folds.title: Four simple habits
points: A few habits make most prompts better.
None needs special words or tricks.
Meet each one, then see it at work.

folds.title: Show an example
points: Paste one sample of what you like, such as a past email.
Say "write it like this".
Claude copies a style far better from an example than from a description.

chat.you: Write a book club invite. Match the tone of last year's: "Books, snacks and gossip! Join us Friday at 7."

chat.claude: Pages, pastries and plot twists! Join us Saturday at 6.

chat.you: Describe my blue mug in the same style as this: "Sunny yellow, holds a big coffee, loves a slow morning."

chat.claude: Ocean blue, holds a hot tea, loves a quiet evening.

chat.you: Here are last week's meeting notes. Write this week's in the same format.

chat.claude: Done: the same headings, Decisions, Actions and Next steps, with this week's points.

more.note: An example shows a format faster than a description.

folds.title: Ask for steps
points: For a tricky question or a budget, say "work through it step by step".
Claude shows its working.
So you can spot a wrong turn.

folds.title: Asking for steps

chat.you: I earn 2,000 a month and spend 1,700. Step by step: can I save 500?

chat.claude: 1. That leaves 300. 2. 500 is 200 more. 3. Not yet: trim 200 of spending first.

folds.note: Each step is easy to check.

chat.you: Dinner cost 90. Sam pays 10 extra for wine. Split the rest between three of us, step by step.

chat.claude: 1. 90 minus 10 is 80. 2. 80 split three ways is about 26.67 each. 3. Sam pays about 36.67.

chat.you: Can I paint two rooms this weekend? Each takes 6 hours, plus 2 to dry. Step by step.

chat.claude: 1. Painting takes 12 hours. 2. One room dries while you paint the other. 3. Yes, if you start early Saturday.

more.note: Steps show how Claude got there.

folds.title: Add structure
points: Put long material in clear, labelled blocks.
Like "Here is my draft:" then "Here is what I want changed:".
It stops Claude mixing them up.

folds.title: Adding structure
points: **My draft:** paste the letter here.
**What to change:** shorter and friendlier.
**Keep:** the date and the address.
folds.note: Claude knows which part is which.

points: **My CV:** paste it here.
**The job ad:** paste it here.
**What I want:** three ways to make my CV fit this job.
more.note: Two long texts, clearly kept apart.

points: **Meeting notes:** paste them here.
**Questions:** What did we decide? Who does what by Friday?
**Format:** a short list.
more.note: Claude answers from the notes, not from guesses.

folds.title: Iterate
points: Your first prompt is a first try.
Read the answer, then say what to change.
Chatting back and forth is the normal way to work.

chat.you: Suggest a name for my bakery.
Nice! Something warmer, with my name, Rosa.

chat.claude: A watch, a book or a nice wallet?

chat.you: He loves gardening and hates clutter.

chat.claude: A garden centre voucher, or a day out at a famous garden?

more.note: Each round adds what Claude needs to know.

chat.you: A slogan for my bike repair shop.

chat.claude: Expert bike repairs at fair prices.

more.note: Say what to change, then try again.

folds.prompt: Tap each card to flip it from weak to strong.

cards.weak: Write an email to my landlord.
cards.strong: Write a polite email to my landlord about a leaking tap. Here is an email I wrote before, copy its friendly tone: ...
Here is my monthly budget: ... Go through it step by step and tell me where I overspend.
cards.note: Asks for steps and labels the material.
